chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Regarding the shortening of the prayer, he said, 'A barid within a barid, four and twenty miles.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: Shortening (of the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs)
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: A traditional unit of distance (approx. 6 miles)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific distance in miles required to shorten prayers during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the travel distance for qasr as twenty-four miles, a measurement derived from the 'barid' unit used in the Umayyad postal system, which was approximately 4,000 cubits. This narration is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the minimum distance (masafat al-taqseer) required to shorten the four-rak'ah prayers, reflecting the practical legal standards of the early Islamic community.
